sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: Alright, turning on to South Temple Road.
sentences.zh: 好了，转入南圣殿路。

sentences.en: Road?
sentences.zh: 路？

sentences.en: Place?
sentences.zh: 还是广场？

sentences.en: It's just called South Temple.
sentences.zh: 它就叫南圣殿。

sentences.en: South Temple is in fact the complete name of the street on which our producer Sam Greenspan is driving.
sentences.zh: “南圣殿”实际上就是我们制片人萨姆·格林斯潘正在行驶的那条街道的全名。

sentences.en: Crossing 500 EaSt.
sentences.zh: 穿过东500街。

sentences.en: Exactly 660 feet later, Sam drives across the next major street.
sentences.zh: 正好660英尺后，萨姆穿过了下一条主干道。

sentences.en: Here's 400 EaSt.
sentences.zh: 这是东400街。

sentences.en: And 660 feet after that.
sentences.zh: 再过660英尺。

sentences.en: 300 EaSt.
If you recognize the streets that Sam is calling off, you already know exactly where he is and what he's about to see.
sentences.zh: 如果你认得萨姆报出的这些街道，你就已经确切地知道他在哪里，以及他即将看到什么了。

sentences.en: 200 EaSt.
And now here's State Street, which seems to work like a 100 EaSt.
sentences.zh: 现在是州街，它似乎起到了东100街的作用。

sentences.en: Wow, there it is.
sentences.zh: 哇，就在那儿。

sentences.en: Oh my gosh.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: That is the Mormon Temple.
sentences.zh: 那就是摩门圣殿。

sentences.en: The Salt Lake Temple of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints in Salt Lake City, Utah.
sentences.zh: 位于犹他州盐湖城的耶稣基督后期圣徒教会的盐湖城圣殿。

sentences.en: It's quite striking.
sentences.zh: 非常引人注目。

sentences.en: It's beautiful.
sentences.zh: 太美了。

sentences.en: The urban grid of Salt Lake City, Utah is designed to tell you exactly where you are in relation to Temple Square, one of the holiest sites for Mormons.
sentences.zh: 犹他州盐湖城的城市网格设计，是为了让你确切地知道自己相对于圣殿广场的位置，那是摩门教最神圣的地点之一。

sentences.en: I first learned about this when I was writing a letter to a friend in Salt Lake whose address was like 300-something South, 2100 East, Salt Lake City, UT.
sentences.zh: 我第一次了解到这一点时，是正在给盐湖城的一位朋友写信，地址大概是盐湖城南300街，东2100街。

sentences.en: Which to me sounded less like a specific house number and more like a set of coordinates.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这听起来不像是一个具体的门牌号，更像是一组坐标。

sentences.en: But that's pretty much how every address works in Salt Lake City and in Utah generally.
sentences.zh: 但这基本上就是盐湖城乃至整个犹他州所有地址的运作方式。

sentences.en: 300 South, 2100 East means three blocks south and 21 blocks east of Temple Square.
sentences.zh: 南300街，东2100街意味着距离圣殿广场南边三个街区，东边21个街区。

sentences.en: But the most striking thing about Salt Lake's grid to us non-Utauns is the scale.
sentences.zh: 但对于我们这些非犹他州人来说，盐湖城网格最引人注目的地方在于它的规模。

sentences.en: Each block is 660 feet on each side.
sentences.zh: 每个街区每边长660英尺。

sentences.en: That means you're walking more than two football fields to get from one intersection to the next.
sentences.zh: 这意味着你得走过两个多足球场的距离才能从一个路口到达下一个路口。

sentences.en: Salt Lake's blocks are the biggest in the country.
sentences.zh: 盐湖城的街区是全国最大的。

sentences.en: You can fit nine Portland, Oregon blocks inside one of Salt Lake City's.
sentences.zh: 你可以在盐湖城的一个街区里塞进九个俄勒冈州波特兰市的街区。

sentences.en: These giant blocks have created some challenges for the city of Salt Lake.
sentences.zh: 这些巨大的街区给盐湖城市带来了一些挑战。

sentences.en: But they were all part of the original plan for the city.
sentences.zh: 但它们都是该市最初规划的一部分。

sentences.en: One created by its Mormon founders a century and a half ago in an effort to create a spiritual utopia in the desert.
sentences.zh: 这是由其摩门教创始人在一个半世纪前为了在沙漠中建立一个精神乌托邦而设计的。

sentences.en: Every city plan begins as someone's utopia.
sentences.zh: 每个城市规划最初都是某人的乌托邦。

sentences.en: Urban planners imagine the way their city ought to be, make some drawings, and then watch as that vision becomes reality.
sentences.zh: 城市规划者构想出他们心目中城市应有的样子，画出草图，然后看着那个愿景成为现实。

sentences.en: Throughout most of human civilization, urban planners imagine their cities arising from a system of streets joining at right angles.
sentences.zh: 在人类文明的大部分时间里，城市规划者都设想他们的城市是由直角相交的街道系统组成的。

sentences.en: A grid.
sentences.zh: 一个网格。

sentences.en: The idea of a grid goes back at least to 2600 BC in the Indus Valley in what is now Pakistan and northwest India.
sentences.zh: 网格的概念至少可以追溯到公元前2600年的印度河流域，即现在的巴基斯坦和印度西北部。

sentences.en: We know this from archaeological findings.
sentences.zh: 我们从考古发现中得知这一点。

sentences.en: Ancient Egypt had grids.
sentences.zh: 古埃及有网格。

sentences.en: Ancient Babylonia had grids.
sentences.zh: 古巴比伦有网格。

sentences.en: The Greeks and the Romans had grids.
sentences.zh: 希腊人和罗马人也有网格。

sentences.en: Many cities in Europe don't have a grid.
sentences.zh: 欧洲的许多城市没有网格。

sentences.en: But when European settlers came to North America, they mostly built gridiron cities.
sentences.zh: 但当欧洲定居者来到北美时，他们大多建造了网格状城市。

sentences.en: When Joseph Smith, founder of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, the religion of the Mormons, first conceived of a holy city for his new religion,
sentences.zh: 当耶稣基督后期圣徒教会（即摩门教）的创始人约瑟夫·史密斯首次为他的新宗教构想一座圣城时，

sentences.en: he would not have had much experience with large urban grids.
sentences.zh: 他并没有太多大型城市网格的经验。

sentences.en: He was born in New England, and then when he was young, his family lived to upstate New York.
sentences.zh: 他出生在新英格兰，年轻时全家搬到了纽约州北部。

sentences.en: He never would have saw a city that had more than a couple thousand residents.
sentences.zh: 他从未见过居民超过几千人的城市。

sentences.en: This is Dr. Benjamin Park.
sentences.zh: 这位是本杰明·帕克博士。

sentences.en: My name is Benjamin Park.
sentences.zh: 我叫本杰明·帕克。

sentences.en: I am an assistant professor of American religious history at Sam Houston State University.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆休斯顿州立大学美国宗教史的助理教授。

sentences.en: Dr. Park says that Joseph Smith's foray into urban planning began with a document called The Platte of Zion.
sentences.zh: 帕克博士说，约瑟夫·史密斯在城市规划方面的尝试始于一份名为《锡安规划图》的文件。

sentences.en: The Platte of Zion was a map that details all the way down to how big the housing plots would be,
sentences.zh: 《锡安规划图》是一张详细说明了住房地块大小的地图，

sentences.en: how many roads would fit into the city, where the courthouse would be, where the temples will be,
sentences.zh: 包括城市能容纳多少道路、法院在哪里、圣殿在哪里，

sentences.en: how many people will live within these boundaries.
sentences.zh: 以及这些边界内将居住多少人。

sentences.en: It's a plan which Mormons believe came to their prophet Joseph Smith,
sentences.zh: 这是一个摩门教徒相信是他们的先知约瑟夫·史密斯所领受的规划，

sentences.en: part and parcel with a series of revelations that led him to found the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints,
sentences.zh: 伴随着一系列启示，引导他创立了耶稣基督后期圣徒教会，

sentences.en: a plan which would inspire the Mormons' eventual spiritual home in the Salt Lake Valley.
sentences.zh: 这一规划最终激励了摩门教徒在盐湖谷建立了他们的精神家园。

sentences.en: Have you been in the Temple Square before?
sentences.zh: 你以前来过圣殿广场吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I was here yesterday.
sentences.zh: 是的，我昨天来过。

sentences.en: I was walking around.
sentences.zh: 我到处走了走。

sentences.en: I got to see some of the sites.
sentences.zh: 我参观了一些景点。

sentences.en: So we don't have to point out which is the tabernacle, which is the temple?
sentences.zh: 所以我们不需要指出哪个是会幕，哪个是圣殿了？

sentences.en: Feel free to.
sentences.zh: 请随意。

sentences.en: It makes good radio.
sentences.zh: 这会是很好的广播素材。

sentences.en: Showing Sam around Temple Square is Keith Erickson, director of the LDS Church History Library.
sentences.zh: 带领萨姆参观圣殿广场的是耶稣基督后期圣徒教会历史图书馆馆长基思·埃里克森。

sentences.en: Accompanying them is Emily Utt, historic sites curator for the LDS Church.
sentences.zh: 陪同他们的是耶稣基督后期圣徒教会的历史遗迹策展人艾米丽·乌特。

sentences.en: See, I could go on for about three weeks about Temple Square.
sentences.zh: 你看，关于圣殿广场我可以讲上三个星期。

sentences.en: Keith and Emily took Sam to the LDS Church History Museum.
sentences.zh: 基思和艾米丽带萨姆去了耶稣基督后期圣徒教会历史博物馆。

sentences.en: So we'll just kind of speed through the exhibit and find it.
sentences.zh: 所以我们还是快速浏览一下展览，找到它吧。

sentences.en: The plat itself is over here.
sentences.zh: 规划图就在这边。

sentences.en: So this is it.
sentences.zh: 就是这个。

sentences.en: This is the original.
sentences.zh: 这是原件。

sentences.en: This is what they described and named the Plat of Zion.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们描述并命名为《锡安规划图》的东西。

sentences.en: The three of us are gathered around a display case in the museum
sentences.zh: 我们三个人围在博物馆的一个展示柜旁，

sentences.en: that's actually pretty easy to just walk right paSt.
sentences.zh: 实际上很容易就直接走过去了。

sentences.en: I actually think the display case here understates the significance of what's in it.
sentences.zh: 我其实觉得这里的展示柜低估了其中展品的重要性。

sentences.en: It's just a rough-hewn, you know, it's designed to look like a rough-hewn wood box.
sentences.zh: 它只是一个粗糙的，你知道，设计成看起来像一个粗糙的木箱子。

sentences.en: Inside, under thick museum glass, is a large piece of parchment with Joseph Smith's urban plan for an American city of God.
sentences.zh: 在里面，厚厚的博物馆玻璃下，是一大块羊皮纸，上面有约瑟夫·史密斯为上帝之城设计的城市规划。

sentences.en: The temple blocks in the middle are kind of this ochre, kind of red color,
sentences.zh: 中间的圣殿街区是一种赭石色，有点像红色，

sentences.en: and then the streets are labeled in a kind of a light green.
sentences.zh: 然后街道用一种浅绿色标出。

sentences.en: The document we're all looking at, the Plat of Zion, is a city plan,
sentences.zh: 我们正在看的这份文件，《锡安规划图》，是一份城市规划，

sentences.en: a series of squares divided up by horizontal and vertical lines.
sentences.zh: 一系列由水平和垂直线条分割的方块。

sentences.en: It is one of the first documents that the Mormon prophet Joseph Smith and his scribes produced.
sentences.zh: 这是摩门教先知约瑟夫·史密斯和他的书记员制作的最早的文件之一。

sentences.en: It's a pretty simple system.
sentences.zh: 这是一个相当简单的系统。

sentences.en: Very large blocks, 660 feet on each side, all forming right angles with one another.
sentences.zh: 非常大的街区，每边660英尺，彼此之间都形成直角。

sentences.en: All of them the same, except for these special blocks in the middle,
sentences.zh: 除了中间这些特殊的街区外，所有街区都一样，

sentences.en: which he imagined would hold 24 temples.
sentences.zh: 他设想那里将容纳24座圣殿。

sentences.en: The city's grid was designed so that you would always know exactly how far you were from its spiritual center.
sentences.zh: 城市网格的设计是为了让你随时确切地知道自己距离精神中心有多远。

sentences.en: I see these definitely as divinely inspired.
sentences.zh: 我绝对认为这些是神圣启示的产物。

sentences.en: These are coming from a man who had never seen a big city,
sentences.zh: 这些来自一个从未见过大城市的人，

sentences.en: who had probably never heard of city planning,
sentences.zh: 一个可能从未听说过城市规划的人，

sentences.en: and was really looking at this as the basis of a revelation
sentences.zh: 他确实将其视为启示的基础，

sentences.en: to understand how the kingdom of God looks when it hits the earth.
sentences.zh: 以理解上帝的国度降临人间时是什么样子。

sentences.en: This Zionic city that Joseph Smith imagined would be as big as New York or Philadelphia or Boston were at the time.
sentences.zh: 约瑟夫·史密斯构想的这座锡安城，规模将与当时的纽约、费城或波士顿一样大。

sentences.en: It would be an attempt to harness the best things a city could offer,
sentences.zh: 这将是一次尝试，旨在利用城市所能提供的最好东西，

sentences.en: infrastructure, education, community,
sentences.zh: 基础设施、教育、社区，

sentences.en: but without the less savory bits, like vice and crime.
sentences.zh: 但剔除掉那些不太好的部分，比如罪恶和犯罪。

sentences.en: Joseph Smith sought to achieve this by giving people lots of space.
sentences.zh: 约瑟夫·史密斯试图通过给人们提供充足的空间来实现这一点。

sentences.en: It would effectively be a rural city.
sentences.zh: 它实际上将是一座乡村城市。

sentences.en: Within the large blocks, each church member would have a plot of land to have fruit trees and vegetable gardens.
sentences.zh: 在巨大的街区内，每位教会成员都将拥有一块土地，可以种植果树和蔬菜园。

sentences.en: And Joseph Smith imagined the essential piece of the urban fabric would be the home.
sentences.zh: 约瑟夫·史密斯设想城市结构的基本组成部分将是家庭。

sentences.en: Again, Dr. Benjamin Park.
sentences.zh: 再次请出本杰明·帕克博士。

sentences.en: I think he would have rejected the general separation of commercial and domestic living.
sentences.zh: 我认为他会拒绝商业和家庭生活的一般性分离。

sentences.en: You would go to a shop that's based out of someone's home.
sentences.zh: 你会去一家基于某人家庭的商店。

sentences.en: But Smith never got to experience his mixed-use, walkable, everything, artisanally crafted utopian community.
sentences.zh: 但史密斯从未能体验到他那混合用途、适合步行、万事俱备、手工打造的乌托邦社区。

sentences.en: After leading his converts to Ohio and then Missouri and then Illinois,
sentences.zh: 在带领他的皈依者前往俄亥俄州，然后是密苏里州，接着是伊利诺伊州，

sentences.en: and clashing violently with locals pretty much everywhere they went,
sentences.zh: 并且几乎在他们所到之处都与当地人发生暴力冲突之后，

sentences.en: Joseph Smith was killed by an angry anti-Mormon mob in 1844.
sentences.zh: 约瑟夫·史密斯于1844年被一群愤怒的反摩门教暴徒杀害。

sentences.en: The leadership of the LDS church fell to a member of Smith's inner circle,
sentences.zh: 耶稣基督后期圣徒教会的领导权落到了史密斯核心圈子的一名成员手中，

sentences.en: a man named Brigham Young.
sentences.zh: 一个名叫杨百翰的人。

sentences.en: Brigham Young leads a large number of the church out west to what was then Mexican territory.
sentences.zh: 杨百翰带领大量教会成员向西前往当时属于墨西哥的领土。

sentences.en: After a journey spanning years, the Mormons entered the Salt Lake Valley in 1847 and established Salt Lake City.
sentences.zh: 经过数年的旅程，摩门教徒于1847年进入盐湖谷并建立了盐湖城。

sentences.en: It would be the first place that they could build exactly as they wanted.
sentences.zh: 这将是他们能够完全按照自己意愿建造的第一个地方。

sentences.en: And when Brigham Young began devising a plan for what they would build,
sentences.zh: 当杨百翰开始为他们要建造的东西制定计划时，

sentences.en: he returned to Joseph Smith's Platt of Zion.
sentences.zh: 他回到了约瑟夫·史密斯的《锡安规划图》。

sentences.en: Brigham Young's plan does look a bit like Joseph Smith's Platt of Zion, but with more detail and some changes.
sentences.zh: 杨百翰的计划确实看起来有点像约瑟夫·史密斯的《锡安规划图》，但有更多的细节和一些改动。

sentences.en: I see this utopian idea hitting some problems when you have to start dealing with actual landscape.
sentences.zh: 我看到这个乌托邦式的想法在必须开始处理实际景观时遇到了一些问题。

sentences.en: That's Emily Ut again with the LDS church.
sentences.zh: 那是耶稣基督后期圣徒教会的艾米丽·乌特。

sentences.en: Brigham Young realized quickly that the Platt of Zion wouldn't work in the real world without some modifications.
sentences.zh: 杨百翰很快意识到，如果不进行一些修改，《锡安规划图》在现实世界中是行不通的。

sentences.en: Smith's plan called for 24 temples at the center of the city.
sentences.zh: 史密斯的计划要求在城市中心建造24座圣殿。

sentences.en: Young decided to start with one.
sentences.zh: 杨百翰决定从一座开始。

sentences.en: Brigham Young also realized that the city couldn't survive on cottage industries alone.
sentences.zh: 杨百翰也意识到，这座城市不能仅靠家庭手工业生存。

sentences.en: They would also need some commercial and industrial districts.
sentences.zh: 他们还需要一些商业和工业区。

sentences.en: There were limits to the rural city idea,
sentences.zh: 乡村城市的想法是有局限性的，

sentences.en: and the mountainous terrain of the Salt Lake Valley didn't lend itself to a regular rigid grid.
sentences.zh: 而且盐湖谷的山区地形也不适合规则、僵化的网格。

sentences.en: But in many ways, Brigham Young's plan for Salt Lake City is faithful to the Platt of Zion.
sentences.zh: 但在许多方面，杨百翰的盐湖城规划忠实于《锡安规划图》。

sentences.en: The city is still, after all, built around a temple square and with streets named in a way that tell you exactly how far you are from it at all times.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，这座城市仍然围绕着一个圣殿广场而建，街道的命名方式让你随时都能确切地知道自己离它有多远。

sentences.en: And the orderliness of the grid dovetails with Mormon sensibilities about the spiritual importance of maintaining a tidy home.
sentences.zh: 而且网格的有序性与摩门教关于保持家庭整洁的精神重要性的观念相吻合。

sentences.en: Brigham Young and his fellow Mormons did not stop with Salt Lake City.
sentences.zh: 杨百翰和他的摩门教同胞并没有止步于盐湖城。

sentences.en: Over the next half century, they built about 700 towns based on a similar plan all over Utah.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的半个世纪里，他们在犹他州各地建立了大约700个基于类似规划的城镇。

sentences.en: And in many of these towns, they kept Joseph Smith's prescription for large city blocks, 660 feet on each side, with wide streets between them.
sentences.zh: 在这些城镇中，许多都保留了约瑟夫·史密斯关于大型街区的规定，即每边660英尺，中间有宽阔的街道。

sentences.en: The joke is you could turn a wagon around in the middle of the block.
sentences.zh: 有个笑话是说你可以在街区中间调转马车。

sentences.en: Actually, one version of the joke I heard is that the streets are wide enough to be able to turn a wagon around without the drivers resorting to cursing.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我听到的一个版本是，街道足够宽，可以让马车掉头而无需车夫诉诸咒骂。

sentences.en: Knowing Mormons, that's probably very true.
sentences.zh: 了解摩门教徒的话，这很可能是真的。

sentences.en: In Salt Lake City, the wide streets and huge blocks have the effect of making you feel kind of small.
sentences.zh: 在盐湖城，宽阔的街道和巨大的街区会让你感到自己很渺小。

sentences.en: They say that everything is bigger in Texas.
sentences.zh: 人们常说德克萨斯州什么都大。

sentences.en: I just don't think those people have been to Utah before.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得那些人以前没来过犹他州。

sentences.en: This is Molly O'Neill Robinson, urban designer for the Salt Lake City government.
sentences.zh: 这位是莫莉·奥尼尔·罗宾逊，盐湖城市政府的城市设计师。

sentences.en: We're walking around downtown Salt Lake, and she's showing me just how hostile these wide streets can feel to pedestrians.
sentences.zh: 我们正在盐湖城市中心走动，她向我展示了这些宽阔的街道对行人来说是多么不友好。

sentences.en: We are crossing the street right now.
sentences.zh: 我们现在正在过马路。

sentences.en: We're crossing 4th South, also known as 400 South.
sentences.zh: 我们正在穿过南4街，也称为东400街。

sentences.en: So we were given 27 seconds to cross a 132-foot right-of-way.
sentences.zh: 所以我们只有27秒的时间穿过一条132英尺宽的道路。

sentences.en: The blinking pedestrian sign gives us less than half a minute to cross six lanes of traffic.
sentences.zh: 闪烁的行人信号灯只给我们不到半分钟的时间穿过六条车道。

sentences.en: We're walking at a normal pace, not enough time to cross.
sentences.zh: 我们以正常速度行走，时间不够过马路。

sentences.en: Many, if not most, streets in Salt Lake City, even streets in the heart of downtown, are four or six lanes wide.
sentences.zh: 盐湖城的许多街道，甚至市中心的街道，都有四到六条车道宽。

sentences.en: All because the Platte of Zion called for streets with a width of 132 feet.
sentences.zh: 这一切都是因为《锡安规划图》要求街道宽度为132英尺。

sentences.en: Back in the day, things were platted and measured using the surveyor's chain.
sentences.zh: 在过去，土地规划和测量使用的是测量员的链条。

sentences.en: The surveyor's chain is 66 feet, also known as one furlong.
sentences.zh: 测量员的链条是66英尺，也称为一弗隆。

sentences.en: The width of our street is two furlongs, which is 132 feet.
sentences.zh: 我们街道的宽度是两个浪（furlong），也就是132英尺。

sentences.en: The streets are so menacing to cross that the city tried making them safer by offering pedestrians bright orange flags.
sentences.zh: 这些街道过马路时非常危险，所以城市试图通过向行人提供亮橙色旗帜来提高安全性。

sentences.en: So basically, we have a lamppoSt. There is a bucket affixed to it, kind of out of plastic.
sentences.zh: 基本上，我们这儿有个灯柱，上面固定着一个桶，塑料做的。

sentences.en: And there's like one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight.
sentences.zh: 大概有一、二、三、四、五、六、七、八个。

sentences.en: They're pretty big.
sentences.zh: 它们挺大的。

sentences.en: You're supposed to pick up a flag and carry the flag with you as you cross the street for added visibility.
sentences.zh: 你应该拿上一面旗子，过马路时随身带着，以增加可见度。

sentences.en: Should we do it?
sentences.zh: 我们要试一下吗？

sentences.en: We should.
sentences.zh: 我们应该试试。

sentences.en: And I'm going to make you do it because...
sentences.zh: 而且我要让你去试，因为……

sentences.en: You're embarrassed?
sentences.zh: 你觉得尴尬？

sentences.en: No, I refuse to carry a flag.
sentences.zh: 不，我拒绝拿旗子。

sentences.en: All right, so we're crossing now.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那我们现在过马路。

sentences.en: I am waving this flag.
sentences.zh: 我正在挥舞这面旗子。

sentences.en: I've seen these crossing flags in other places.
sentences.zh: 我在其他地方见过这种过街旗。

sentences.en: My neighborhood actually has them at the intersections near the elementary school.
sentences.zh: 我住的社区在小学附近的十字路口就有这种旗子。

sentences.en: But it does seem kind of absurd to ask people to carry bright orange flags in the downtown of a large American city.
sentences.zh: 但在美国大城市的市中心要求人们拿着亮橙色的旗子过马路，确实显得有点荒谬。

sentences.en: We made it across, and I'm going to drop this in the other bucket.
sentences.zh: 我们过来了，我要把旗子放进对面的桶里。

sentences.en: So you refuse to carry these.
sentences.zh: 所以你拒绝拿这些旗子。

sentences.en: So I refuse to carry the flag on principle.
sentences.zh: 我原则上拒绝携带这种旗子。

sentences.en: And I believe that our streets should be designed to inherently make pedestrian crossing safe.
sentences.zh: 我相信我们的街道设计本身就应该让行人过马路变得安全。

sentences.en: And if you have to carry a flag across the street to get someone to notice you, then we haven't designed the street safely.
sentences.zh: 如果你必须拿着旗子过马路才能引起别人的注意，那就说明我们的街道设计得不够安全。

sentences.en: And difficulty crossing the street is not the only problem with large blocks.
sentences.zh: 而且过马路困难并不是大街区带来的唯一问题。

sentences.en: Urban planners have long known that short blocks are inherently more interesting
sentences.zh: 城市规划者早就知道，短街区天生就更有趣，

sentences.en: because there's a greater density of what they call network nodes or sites of possible interaction between people.
sentences.zh: 因为它们有更高密度的所谓“网络节点”，也就是人们之间可能产生互动的地方。

sentences.en: Shorter blocks mean more intersections, and more intersections mean more options for what to do or where to go.
sentences.zh: 更短的街区意味着更多的十字路口，而更多的十字路口意味着更多的选择，无论是做什么还是去哪里。

sentences.en: Given the problems that large blocks and wide streets have created in Salt Lake,
sentences.zh: 鉴于盐湖城的大街区和宽街道所带来的问题，

sentences.en: you might get the idea that Salt Lake's founders just started out with a bad plan.
sentences.zh: 你可能会觉得盐湖城的创始人们一开始就制定了一个糟糕的规划。

sentences.en: Not at all.
sentences.zh: 完全不是这样。

sentences.en: Oh, no.
sentences.zh: 噢，不。

sentences.en: What you're seeing there is a complete misunderstanding of Brigham Young's conception.
sentences.zh: 你所看到的完全是对杨百翰（Brigham Young）构想的误解。

sentences.en: That's Andres Duwani, a partner with the architecture firm DPZ.
sentences.zh: 那是安德烈斯·杜瓦尼（Andres Duany），建筑事务所DPZ的合伙人。

sentences.en: He's also one of the founders of the New Urbanist Movement,
sentences.zh: 他也是“新城市主义运动”的创始人之一，

sentences.en: which seeks to make cities and suburbs less car-oriented, more walkable, and more environmentally friendly.
sentences.zh: 该运动旨在使城市和郊区减少对汽车的依赖，更适合步行，且更环保。

sentences.en: Andres Duwani says that in Brigham Young's original plan,
sentences.zh: 安德烈斯·杜瓦尼说，在杨百翰最初的规划中，

sentences.en: the streets were never supposed to be paved from curb to curb.
sentences.zh: 街道从来就没打算从路缘石到路缘石全部铺上路面。

sentences.en: The streets were basically a green space,
sentences.zh: 街道基本上是绿地，

sentences.en: with pavement only in the parts where settlers wanted the ox carts to go.
sentences.zh: 只有定居者需要牛车通行的地方才铺设路面。

sentences.en: And Brigham Young never imagined that the huge blocks originally meant for farming
sentences.zh: 而且杨百翰从未想过，那些最初用于耕作的巨大街区，

sentences.en: would remain intact as the city evolved.
sentences.zh: 会随着城市的发展而保持原样。

sentences.en: He understood that the blocks would have to be subdivided from agricultural to urban over time.
sentences.zh: 他明白，随着时间的推移，这些街区必须从农业用地细分为城市用地。

sentences.en: For Duwani, the Salt Lake City we have today represents the stagnation of Brigham Young's dream.
sentences.zh: 对杜瓦尼来说，我们今天看到的盐湖城代表了杨百翰梦想的停滞。

sentences.en: So Salt Lake City went from the most beautiful to actually among the most hostile in the WeSt.
sentences.zh: 所以盐湖城从最美丽的城市变成了西部最不友好的城市之一。

sentences.en: And that's a misunderstanding of the intention of Brigham Young and the Platte of Zion.
sentences.zh: 而这正是对杨百翰和“锡安规划”（Platte of Zion）意图的误解。

sentences.en: Making the city less hostile to pedestrians is exactly what anti-orange flag Molly O'Neill Robinson is trying to do.
sentences.zh: 让城市对行人变得友好，正是那位反对橙色旗帜的莫莉·奥尼尔·罗宾逊（Molly O'Neill Robinson）正在努力做的事情。

sentences.en: She wants to take those huge blocks, break them down into more walkable sections,
sentences.zh: 她想把那些巨大的街区拆解成更适合步行的区域，

sentences.en: and make them more interesting.
sentences.zh: 并让它们变得更有趣。

sentences.en: You know, that there's something kind of engaging and delighting your eye as you're moving along.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当你走在路上时，总有一些东西能吸引你的目光，让你感到愉悦。

sentences.en: Molly is hoping to do this block by block in Salt Lake City.
sentences.zh: 莫莉希望在盐湖城逐个街区地实现这一目标。

sentences.en: She took Sam to one current project on Regent Street,
sentences.zh: 她带萨姆（Sam）去了摄政街（Regent Street）的一个当前项目，

sentences.en: where they're working on getting more pedestrian life into the middle of the block.
sentences.zh: 他们正在那里努力让街区中间产生更多的行人活动。

sentences.en: So Regent Street is really the pedestrian first street in Salt Lake.
sentences.zh: 所以摄政街确实是盐湖城第一条以行人优先的街道。

sentences.en: So the street has always been here, but you're kind of redesigning its use?
sentences.zh: 所以这条街一直都在这里，但你们是在重新设计它的用途？

sentences.en: Yes, yes.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的。

sentences.en: Regent Street used to just be an access road for some downtown parking structures.
sentences.zh: 摄政街过去只是市中心一些停车场的通道。

sentences.en: Now it's a pedestrian walkway that opens up into a plaza with a brand new theater, a new restaurant space.
sentences.zh: 现在它变成了一条步行街，通向一个拥有全新剧院和新餐厅空间的广场。

sentences.en: The idea with this street is that we will be able to close down portions of the street for festivals and events,
sentences.zh: 这条街的设计理念是，我们可以封闭街道的部分路段来举办节日和活动，

sentences.en: you know, big theater openings, things like that.
sentences.zh: 你知道，大型剧院开幕式之类的活动。

sentences.en: As of the time of this recording, Regent Street is still under construction.
sentences.zh: 在本期节目录制时，摄政街仍在施工中。

sentences.en: But even so, people are already drawn to walk through it.
sentences.zh: 但即便如此，人们已经被吸引着走过这里了。

sentences.en: The stakes for creating a denser, more walkable Salt Lake are high.
sentences.zh: 打造一个密度更高、更适合步行的盐湖城，其意义重大。

sentences.en: Even though the city feels wide open and nature is easily accessible,
sentences.zh: 尽管这座城市感觉非常开阔，自然环境也触手可及，

sentences.en: Salt Lake suffers from some of the worst air pollution in the country.
sentences.zh: 但盐湖城却遭受着全国最严重的空气污染之一。

sentences.en: The mountain ranges around the city trap in all the smog, which largely comes from cars.
sentences.zh: 城市周围的山脉锁住了所有的烟雾，而这些烟雾主要来自汽车。

sentences.en: What's more, Salt Lake is expected to double in population by 2050,
sentences.zh: 更重要的是，预计到2050年，盐湖城的人口将翻一番，

sentences.en: and it can't expand its city limits because of geographic boundaries,
sentences.zh: 而且由于地理边界的限制，它无法扩大城市边界，

sentences.en: like mountains and a great big salty lake.
sentences.zh: 比如山脉和大盐湖。

sentences.en: The city's ability to thrive will be determined by its ability to make more efficient use of the space it already has.
sentences.zh: 这座城市繁荣发展的能力将取决于它能否更有效地利用现有空间。

sentences.en: There's a lot of optimism in the city for finding better ways to use its large blocks and wide streets.
sentences.zh: 城里对于寻找更好的方式来利用其大街区和宽街道充满了乐观情绪。

sentences.en: And there's been some progress.
sentences.zh: 而且已经取得了一些进展。

sentences.en: But several developers told me that the new city administration has not been kind to these approaches.
sentences.zh: 但几位开发商告诉我，新一届市政府对这些方法并不友好。

sentences.en: They seem to be more about keeping Salt Lake City as it is.
sentences.zh: 他们似乎更倾向于维持盐湖城的现状。

sentences.en: In the Church of Latter-day Saints, there's a principle called continuous revelation,
sentences.zh: 在耶稣基督后期圣徒教会中，有一个原则叫“持续启示”，

sentences.en: that God is still speaking, and that divine truths are still being revealed.
sentences.zh: 即上帝仍在说话，神圣的真理仍在被揭示。

sentences.en: And so maybe what Salt Lake City needs, maybe what all American cities need,
sentences.zh: 所以也许盐湖城所需要的，也许所有美国城市所需要的，

sentences.en: is a kind of continuous revelation,
sentences.zh: 是一种“持续启示”，

sentences.en: a way of honoring the principles on which a city was founded,
sentences.zh: 一种既尊重城市建立之初的原则，

sentences.en: but with the understanding that they must adapt and respond to the demands of the present.
sentences.zh: 又理解必须适应并回应时代需求的方式。
